purpose: The single machine-readable statement of which external implementations this project is allowed to cite as oracles, and what each one is scientifically entitled to say. scripts/lint-oracle-registry.mjs refuses a study that names an oracleId absent from this file, and refuses a study whose claimed role is not among that oracle's roleCapabilities.
whyLineageMatters: Two programs are not two independent implementations when they wrap the same library. A study that counts them twice reports a corroboration it does not have. `lineageGroup` is the field that makes double counting visible: oracles sharing a lineageGroup may corroborate each other, and may never be summed as independent legs.

roleDefinitions.analytic-truth: A closed-form value. Outranks every implementation.
roleDefinitions.generator-truth: Labels assigned when a synthetic scene was constructed. Truth for that scene only.
roleDefinitions.field-ground-truth: Independently surveyed reality. The only role that can support E5.
roleDefinitions.original-algorithm-reference: The implementation the published algorithm was released as. Requires that the candidate implements the same stages.
roleDefinitions.same-algorithm-independent-implementatio: A separate codebase implementing the same published algorithm.
roleDefinitions.independent-same-quantity-implementation: A separate codebase computing the same mathematical quantity by its own route.
roleDefinitions.alternative-algorithm-family: A different algorithm answering a related question. Scored against truth, never used as a conformance gate.
roleDefinitions.standard-conformance-validator: Decides whether an artifact satisfies a format specification. Says nothing about numerical accuracy.
roleDefinitions.independent-statistical-recalculation: Recomputes a statistic outside the candidate's language and runtime.
roleDefinitions.same-lineage-corroboration: Shares an implementation family with another registered oracle. A compatibility check, never a second independent leg.

oracles.name: PROJ
independenceNotes: GDAL links PROJ for coordinate operations, so a GDAL reprojection leg and a PROJ leg share this lineage and must not be counted as two.
Independent of GeographicLib: different codebase, different series formulation, no shared transverse-Mercator code.
limitations: Transformation accuracy depends on which datum grids are installed. A study must record the operation PROJ selected, not only the numbers it printed.
Run from the host toolchain rather than the digest-pinned oracle image, so reproducibility rests on the recorded version string.

oracles.name: GeographicLib
independenceNotes: Karney's own implementation, independent of PROJ. Its transverse Mercator is exact to round-off rather than a truncated Krüger series, which is why it is the stronger of the two for a projection-accuracy bound.
Applies the UTM zone exceptions (Norway 32V, Svalbard 31X/33X/35X/37X) from the UTM definition, so it validates zone selection and not only projection arithmetic.
limitations: GeoConvert refuses exponential-notation input, so fixtures serialize coordinates as fixed decimals.
Run from the host toolchain rather than the digest-pinned oracle image, so reproducibility rests on the recorded version string.

oracles.name: PDAL
independenceNotes: filters.smrf is an independent implementation of Pingel et al. 2013. OLV implements a documented SUBSET of those stages, so the two are same-algorithm only over the stages both implement; the study must say which.
PDAL's E57 reader links libE57Format. Any other libE57Format-based reader shares this lineage.
limitations: writers.gdal with a radius below half the cell size tests cell indexing and origin, not neighbourhood semantics.

oracles.name: GDAL
independenceNotes: Links PROJ for coordinate operations. A GDAL reprojection result and a PROJ result are one lineage, not two.
gdaldem slope/aspect implement Horn, which is the formula OLV registers; that is what makes them same-quantity rather than alternative-family.
limitations: The pinned image installs GDAL 3.13.1; the reference workstation's Homebrew GDAL was later upgraded to 3.13.3, so four host-produced reference-run sets truthfully record 3.13.3. Both patch releases of 3.13.x are declared in validation/oracles/oracle-pins.json (oracleVersions.GDAL) and accepted by scripts/verify-oracle-versions.mjs; a version outside that declared set still fails. Reproduce against 3.13.1 from the pinned image.

oracles.name: GRASS GIS
independenceNotes: Its own raster engine and map algebra, sharing no code with GDAL or PDAL. GRASS links PROJ for coordinate operations, so a GRASS REPROJECTION leg would share the proj lineage; raster algebra and cell statistics do not.
r.mapcalc propagates null the way the candidate propagates NaN, so a cell absent from either epoch is comparable in neither without any special handling on either side.
Computes in double, so on the change fixtures it reproduces the closed-form volumes exactly while the candidate carries float32 storage error.
limitations: r.in.xyz reduces per cell with no neighbourhood radius, so it is an exact-cell oracle and not a substitute for a radius-based writer where that is the quantity under test.
Run from the host conda environment rather than the digest-pinned oracle image, so reproducibility rests on the recorded version string.

oracles.name: SAGA GIS
oracles.installationMethod: not on PATH; validation/cross-implementation/studies/VRM-SAGA-ANALYTIC.study.json records the exact executable the existing leg ran from
independenceNotes: Independent of GDAL for the vector-ruggedness quantity.
limitations: Not resolvable on PATH on the current host, so new SAGA legs are pending until it is installed.
conda-forge publishes no SAGA package for linux-64, so it cannot join the pinned image as things stand.

oracles.name: R
independenceNotes: Recomputes statistics outside the candidate's language and runtime, which is what makes it independent of a TypeScript implementation of the same formula.

Its quantile default is type 7, which interpolates. src/validation/checkpointAccuracy.ts takes the nearest rank, so median, NMAD and P95 differ on even-length samples. A study comparing them must name the convention on each side.
limitations: Validates arithmetic only. A correct recomputation says nothing about whether the underlying error model is calibrated against real terrain.
The host currently carries R 4.6.1. The existing profile study cites 4.4.1, so a study must record the version it actually ran.
The existing profile study cites R 4.4.1. Both versions are recorded by the studies that ran them rather than one being retired.

oracles.name: CloudCompare
oracles.installationMethod: application bundle at /Applications/CloudCompare.app, command line entry point /Applications/CloudCompare.app/Contents/MacOS/CloudCompare
independenceNotes: Nearest-neighbour and cloud-to-cloud distance come from CCCoreLib, its own octree and distance code, which shares no source with GDAL, PROJ, PDAL or GRASS. That is the part of CloudCompare this registry treats as an independent leg.

The bundle ships libgdal.34 and libproj.25 in Contents/Frameworks. Any raster read, raster write or coordinate transformation done through CloudCompare is gdal or proj lineage, not a second leg against the registered gdal-3.13.1 or proj-9.8.1 entries.

The bundle ships PCL 1.14 (libpcl_features, libpcl_registration, libpcl_surface and others) behind the QPCL and QPCL_IO plugins. Anything cited from those plugins, including PCL normal estimation and PCL registration, is pcl lineage and may not be summed with pcl-1.15.1.

The E57 reader is the QE57_IO plugin over libxerces-c, and the LAS reader is QLAS_IO over liblaszip. Whether either shares source with the libE57Format path that pdal-2.10.2 uses was not established here, so an E57 or LAS decode leg from CloudCompare is recorded as unknown independence rather than as an independent leg.
limitations: C2C_DIST picks its octree subdivision level automatically when none is given, and the level it picks is a function of the two clouds. The run recorded here reported "Octree level (auto): 6". A study must record the level and any -MAX_DIST, -SPLIT_XYZ or local-model option, because a different level changes which neighbours are searched and therefore the distances reported.

Default C2C distance is point to nearest point, not point to surface. Against a sampled surface it carries a sampling bias that grows with point spacing, so it is not interchangeable with a local-model or M3C2 distance without saying which was run.

M3C2 answers a different question than raster differencing: it measures along local normals with its own projection and normal scales. It belongs in a study as alternative-algorithm-family, scored against truth, never as a conformance gate on a raster volume.
Requires the cocoa Qt platform plugin. The bundle ships no offscreen plugin, so the binary aborts under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen and cannot run on a headless CI worker as installed.
Run from a host application bundle rather than a digest-pinned oracle image, so reproducibility rests on the recorded version string.

oracles.name: Point Cloud Library
independenceNotes: CloudCompare 2.13.2 bundles PCL 1.14 behind its QPCL plugin. A PCL normal or registration result obtained through CloudCompare and one obtained from these binaries are one lineage. Only CCCoreLib routines make CloudCompare a separate leg.

Neighbour search runs through FLANN (libflann_cpp) rather than PCL source. Any other FLANN-based neighbour search shares that dependency, so a pure nearest-neighbour comparison is weaker evidence than a normals or registration comparison where the estimator itself is PCL code.

Whether the registered pdal-2.10.2 image was built with its optional PCL-backed plugins was not checked here. Until it is, a study pairing PDAL and PCL on a routine PDAL could be delegating must record that independence is unestablished rather than assume it.
Independent of GDAL, PROJ and GRASS: PCL links neither for the routines above.
limitations: pcl_normal_estimation gives a normal an arbitrary sign unless a viewpoint is set. It defaults to the origin, so a comparison against a candidate that orients normals by a different convention must compare unsigned angle or state the orientation rule on both sides.

Passing -radius on an organized dataset silently switches the estimator: the value is reused as the smoothing size of IntegralImageNormalEstimation instead of a neighbourhood radius, and the result is then a different algorithm than the unorganized path. The tool prints both interpretations, and a study must record which one ran.
The command line tools read and write PCD. PCD carries no CRS, so any georeferencing is lost on the round trip and the leg speaks to geometry in the file frame only.
PCD ascii and the default binary form store coordinates as float32, which puts a quantization floor under any comparison on large absolute coordinates.
Run from the host toolchain rather than the digest-pinned oracle image, so reproducibility rests on the recorded version string.

oracles.name: GNU Octave
independenceNotes: Its strongest role is running an author's own MATLAB code released alongside a paper. Doing so makes the comparison original-algorithm-reference rather than one more implementation, but only when the published code is the code that ran. A study must cite the exact script and its provenance, because Octave is the interpreter and not the algorithm.
Where no author code is involved, Octave is an independent recalculation of a formula outside the candidate's language and runtime, in the same sense as r-4.6.1 but a separate codebase from it.

On this host Octave and R both link the same /opt/homebrew/opt/openblas libopenblas.0.dylib. Elementwise statistics such as RMSE, quantiles and NMAD are unaffected, but a dense linear algebra result (least squares, eigen decomposition, matrix inverse) obtained from Octave and from R shares a BLAS and LAPACK path and is not two independent legs.
Octave also links ARPACK and SuiteSparse for eigen and sparse routines. The same caution applies to any leg resting on those.
limitations: MATLAB compatibility is high but not total, and it is toolbox dependent. Core language and base library functions match closely; anything from a MATLAB toolbox is absent unless the corresponding Octave Forge package is installed. On this host only image 2.20.0 is installed, and exist('regionprops') returns 0, so a reference script calling a Statistics, Mapping or Curve Fitting toolbox function will error rather than return a wrong number.

Where a function exists in both, defaults may still differ (integer division and rounding rules, printf handling of some conversions, do-until and other Octave-only syntax that MATLAB will not run). A study running author code must record that the script executed unmodified, or list every edit made to it.

Octave's quantile default is method 5, and its median on even-length samples interpolates. src/validation/checkpointAccuracy.ts takes the nearest rank, so a study comparing them must name the convention on each side, as the r-4.6.1 entry already requires.
Validates arithmetic only. A correct recomputation says nothing about whether the underlying model is calibrated against real terrain.
Run from the host toolchain rather than the digest-pinned oracle image, so reproducibility rests on the recorded version string.

oracles.name: Observatory state-table oracle (state_table.py)
oracles.installationMethod: in-repository; run with the interpreter .python-version pins
independenceNotes: Written from docs/observatory/SPEC.md §2.2-§2.4 and validation/protocols/observatory/OB-ST-THRESHOLDS.protocol.json's boundary rules, not from src/observation/stateTable.ts. Not external validation: both are this project's own documents, so a shared misreading of SPEC would survive agreement between the two implementations. See this file's own module docstring.
limitations: Checks a pure classification function against a bounded, explicitly enumerated lattice of counter combinations (see state-table-lattice.json), not against any real scan.

Shares no code, dependency or lineage with any other registered oracle in this file; the lineageGroup exists so a future in-repository Observatory or SensorPrint oracle that reuses this one's helper functions is recorded as sharing it, rather than counted as a second independent leg.

oracles.name: Observatory ray-AABB clip and voxel traversal oracle (ray_aabb_traversal.py)
oracles.installationMethod: in-repository; run with the interpreter .python-version pins
independenceNotes: Implements Amanatides & Woo (1987) 3D DDA traversal and slab-method AABB clipping directly from their published definitions, stepping in exact rational arithmetic (fractions.Fraction) rather than the floating-point the TypeScript traversal (docs/observatory/SPEC.md OB-LED-01, implemented starting phase O4) will use. The written tie rule for a ray exactly on a voxel face or corner is this oracle's own statement, not a transcription of any TypeScript code, since no TypeScript traversal exists yet.
Shares its lineageGroup with olv-observatory-state-table-py for the reason stated on that entry.
limitations: Checked only against the four analytic F8 cases in validation/observatory/fixtures/f8-dda-cases.json (axis-aligned, along a face, grazing a corner, zero-length), not against a real scan or a general-position ray.

Exact-rational stepping is possible only because every F8 fixture coordinate is deliberately an exactly representable dyadic rational; it says nothing about floating-point behaviour on a ray whose parameters are not.

oracles.name: Observatory shadow-frontier adjacency oracle (shadow_frontier.py)
oracles.installationMethod: in-repository; run with the interpreter .python-version pins
independenceNotes: Written from docs/observatory/SPEC.md §2.4/§5.4's frontier definition directly, not from src/observation/shadowFrontier.ts. Not external validation: both are this project's own documents, so a shared misreading of SPEC would survive agreement between the two implementations. See this file's own module docstring.
Shares its lineageGroup with olv-observatory-state-table-py and olv-observatory-ray-aabb-traversal-py for the reason stated on the first of those entries.
limitations: Checks 6-adjacency over one small, explicitly enumerated 5x3x1 grid (shadow-frontier-grid.json) built to exercise every adjacency kind and several non-adjacent neighbour states, not a grid produced by an actual traversal.
Says nothing about the area figure (`areaSquareMetres`), which is a direct arithmetic multiply the oracle does not separately check.

oracles.name: Observatory observation-strength component oracle (strength.py)
oracles.installationMethod: in-repository; run with the interpreter .python-version pins
independenceNotes: Written from docs/observatory/SPEC.md §2.5's five component definitions directly, not from src/observation/strength.ts. Not external validation: both are this project's own documents, so a shared misreading of SPEC §2.5 would survive agreement between the two implementations. See this file's own module docstring.
Shares its lineageGroup with olv-observatory-state-table-py, olv-observatory-ray-aabb-traversal-py and olv-observatory-shadow-frontier-py for the reason stated on the first of those entries.
limitations: Checks the five closed-form formulas over seven hand-picked, dyadic-or-simple-diagonal cases (strength-lattice.json) chosen to exercise every NaN/degenerate branch (no samples, no hit/pass evidence, no normal supplied, an out-of-band range, a voxel hit only by a pulse's 2nd return), not a statistically representative sample of real hitting-ray geometry.

The multi-return case only exercises the component formulas over a sample set shaped like a 2nd-return-only hit (a sample carrying the OVERLAPPING return's own range, not the ray's primary range); it does not itself drive a real multi-return traversal or returnTable/returnCounts lookup, which is `accumulateStrengthHitSamples`'s own TypeScript-side responsibility, covered instead by `tests/observatoryStrength.test.ts`'s real end-to-end multi-return group.

Does not check `incidence`'s normal-fitting step (`fitNormalFromResidentPoints`'s covariance fit): every case hands the oracle a normal directly, matching how `computeStrengthComponents` itself takes a normal as an argument rather than fitting one internally.

oracles.name: Observatory Coverage Gain and greedy station-suggestion oracle (coverage_gain.py)
oracles.installationMethod: in-repository; run with the interpreter .python-version pins
independenceNotes: Written from docs/observatory/SPEC.md §5.6 and docs/observatory/methods.md's coverage-gain and station-suggestion sections, not from src/observation/coverageGain.ts or stationSuggestion.ts. Traverses planning rays with ray_aabb_traversal.py's own slab clip and Amanatides & Woo traversal in exact rational arithmetic, and sums the gain terms as fractions. Not external validation: both implementations follow this project's own SPEC, so a shared misreading would survive agreement.

Shares its lineageGroup with olv-observatory-state-table-py, olv-observatory-ray-aabb-traversal-py, olv-observatory-shadow-frontier-py and olv-observatory-strength-py for the reason stated on the first of those entries.
limitations: Scores one declared field (validation/observatory/fixtures/f11-coverage-gain.json: F1's wall and room with a pillar, a not-read corner, PARTIAL, CONFLICT and strong and weak SURFACE regions) and three candidates given by position; it does not generate candidates from a field, which tests/observatoryCoverageGain.test.ts covers on the TypeScript side.

Uses the float planning directions math.cos/math.sin produce, converted exactly to fractions. A last-bit difference between the platform libm and the JavaScript engine's trigonometry could move a ray that grazes a voxel corner; the fixture's 5° step keeps every ray off grid axes and 45° diagonals, and the frozen terms matched the TypeScript scorer exactly on the machine that wrote them.
Takes fitted normals as declared per region; it does not check the covariance normal fit.

oracles.name: Terrain evidence GeoTIFF reader (evidence_geotiff.py)
oracles.installationMethod: in-repository; run with the interpreter .python-version pins
independenceNotes: Parses the written file from the TIFF 6.0, OGC GeoTIFF 1.1, GDAL_METADATA and GDAL_NODATA layouts with struct and xml.etree; it imports no viewer code and does not reuse src/terrain/export/demGeoTiff.ts.

Recomputes interpolation distance as the Chebyshev distance and nearest-support distance as the brute-force Euclidean distance to the nearest cell with support_count > 0, the survey-edge distance by its own breadth-first search, and vertical dispersion as the median absolute deviation of the fixture's listed returns; checks the measured, edge-risk and edge-affected cell_state rules. Not external validation: the rules come from this project's own documents, so a shared misreading would survive agreement.
limitations: Checks one synthetic 12 x 10 fixture (validation/terrain-evidence/fixture), not a raster from a real scan; the fixture has a resolved frame, so cell_state 6 (unresolved) is checked only by tests/demEvidence.test.ts.

Vertical dispersion is recomputed from the returns listed in expected.json, which the TypeScript test writes from the same generator that feeds the rasteriser; the oracle does not see the point cloud.
The distance recomputation assumes an open grid, where 8-connected steps equal the Chebyshev distance; it does not model obstacles.
Says nothing about the accuracy of any height, and does not check the low-confidence rule, which depends on the confidence grid the raster does not carry.

oracles.name: Terrain sensitivity GeoTIFF reader (sensitivity_geotiff.py)
oracles.installationMethod: in-repository; run with the interpreter .python-version pins
independenceNotes: Parses the written file from the TIFF 6.0, OGC GeoTIFF 1.1, GDAL_METADATA and GDAL_NODATA layouts with struct and xml.etree; it imports no viewer code and does not reuse src/terrain/export/demGeoTiff.ts or demSensitivity.ts.

Recomputes the range and the member count from the four member height grids listed in expected.json. Not external validation: the rule comes from this project's own protocol, so a shared misreading would survive agreement. Shares its lineageGroup with olv-terrain-evidence-geotiff-py, which it was modelled on.
limitations: Checks one synthetic 5 x 4 fixture (validation/terrain-sensitivity/fixture) with hand-set member grids, not grids from terrain runs on a real scan.
Does not run the ensemble: the member grids are inputs, so the oracle checks the range rule and the file, not the terrain pipeline behind each member.
Says nothing about how close any height is to the ground.
